source_level.note: #11 §8 writes one letter for two quantities: the amplitude gate "F(k²/μ²)" and the cross-section "σ_T(v) = σ₀F(v²/v*²)". With #1's "k = m_χ v_rel/2" and "v* ≡ √2μ/m_χ", k²/μ² = (1/2)v²/v*², and the cross-section goes as the amplitude squared. So the same F needs F(x/2)² = F(x). A short sympy check in the session scratchpad confirms this for the Gaussian and shows it fails for 1/(1+x) and 1/(1+x)². The rational branch of "tail (Gaussian vs rational)" therefore cannot be the same function in both places. No flag covers this; flag 17 concerns the √2 between #1's and #6's exponents. The pages now describe the notation without asserting identity.
